conflict_policy.why: name/version/bin/scripts are the Lattice distribution contract. Take upstream only for genuinely new runtime dependencies, by hand.
EXTRACTION_VERSION gates the incremental re-extraction heal. Both sides bump it independently, so the two values can name different output — the merged value must be higher than either, never a pick.

KERNEL_ABI_VERSION collides: upstream v2 is a 40-byte ref row with a flags byte; Lattice layers extraJson on top for 48. Same number, different layout — the loader's version check would pass while decode mis-reads. After a sync that touches the layout, advance Lattice's number PAST upstream's, and move layout.ts in the same commit.
Lattice ships no standalone installer (BUNDLING.md). Upstream installer targets do not apply.
telemetry is disabled in Lattice; upstream's design notes describe a surface we do not run.
describes the Lattice-owned sensor, not the upstream product.
path_map applies (codegraph-kernel -> lattice-sensor-kernel) and Lattice stages prebuilds where its own loader looks.

notes: absorbed_at records where sensor/ came from. It never moves, and it is NOT the merge base.

synced_at IS the 3-way merge base, and it advances ONLY when a sync lands with zero unresolved conflicts. Using absorbed_at as the base instead makes every hand-resolved conflict re-conflict on the next sync — a resolution would have no way to reach a settled state. A partially applied sync must leave the marker untouched, or the next run silently skips what was never merged.
A sync target must be a descendant of synced_at. Pointing --ref at an older commit would move the marker backwards while the tree stays new.

The rename to LATTICE_SENSOR_* / lattice-sensor is carried as an ordinary local change: git resolves it as ours, so no rename rules are needed. Do not add textual substitution to the sync path — the rename is selective (some CODEGRAPH_* names are deliberately kept) and cannot be reproduced by rules.
lattice_only paths are never deleted by a sync even when absent upstream.

conflict_policy exists so a resolution is decided once, not re-litigated every sync. When a conflict is resolved by hand, add the path and the reason here — an entry that only says 'ours' without a why is worse than none.
